name: Prunes
description: Prunes represent the naturally dehydrated drupe fruits of Prunus domestica, functioning as a highly concentrated carbohydrate-mineral matrix and a recognized therapeutic agent for gastrointestinal and skeletal homeostasis. Structurally, the dehydration process condenses a unique profile of natural hexoses, bioactive sugar alcohols like sorbitol, and complex non-starch polysaccharides. This botanical architecture is enriched with osteotropic micronutrients, notably phylloquinone and bioavailable boron, alongside a robust array of antioxidant phenolic compounds such as neochlorogenic and chlorogenic acids. Operating as a metabolic modulator, this functional superfood directly stimulates large intestine motility, actively suppresses osteoclast-mediated bone resorption, and neutralizes systemic oxidative stress cascades.
macroIntro: The macronutrient architecture is dominated by a dense, low-moisture carbohydrate matrix containing specific sugar alcohols, complemented by minimal nitrogenous and lipid fractions.
microIntro: An exceptionally concentrated reservoir of essential osteotropic vitamins, intracellular electrolytes, and active polyphenolic antioxidants.

macroNutrients.name: Calories
macroNutrients.description: Substantial thermodynamic energy density originating from the metabolic oxidation of concentrated simple carbohydrates and specific sugar alcohols.

macroNutrients.name: Total Carbohydrates
macroNutrients.description: A complex botanical saccharide blend featuring free D-glucose, D-fructose, and substantial quantities of the sugar alcohol D-glucitol.

macroNutrients.name: Protein
macroNutrients.description: Trace amounts of functional plant proteins and free amino acids embedded within the cellular matrix of the fruit pulp.

macroNutrients.name: Total Fat
macroNutrients.description: Extremely low lipid content, consisting primarily of structural membrane phospholipids and surface epicuticular waxes.

microNutrients.name: Dietary Fiber
microNutrients.description: A synergistic network of soluble pectins and insoluble cellulose that provides mechanical bulk and serves as a primary fermentation substrate for colonic microflora.

microNutrients.name: Sorbitol (D-Glucitol)
microNutrients.description: A poorly absorbed naturally occurring sugar alcohol that exerts potent osmotic pressure in the intestinal lumen, drawing water into the colon.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin K (Phylloquinone)
microNutrients.description: A critical fat-soluble coenzyme essential for the gamma-carboxylation of osteocalcin, driving the crystallization of calcium into the bone matrix.

microNutrients.name: Potassium
microNutrients.description: A dominant intracellular cation vital for maintaining transmembrane resting potentials, regulating myocardial repolarization, and suppressing urinary calcium excretion.

microNutrients.name: Copper
microNutrients.description: An essential transition metal cofactor necessary for lysyl oxidase activity, which cross-links collagen and elastin in structural tissues.

microNutrients.name: Manganese
microNutrients.description: A crucial trace mineral that acts as a cofactor for superoxide dismutase, directly neutralizing mitochondrial oxidative free radicals.

microNutrients.name: Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine)
microNutrients.description: A vital water-soluble coenzyme that drives gluconeogenesis, amino acid transamination, and the synthesis of core central nervous system transmitters.

microNutrients.name: Magnesium
microNutrients.description: A fundamental intracellular divalent cation required for regulating neurochemical stress responses, physical muscle relaxation, and enzymatic ATP utilization.

healthBenefits: Sorbitol-Mediated Osmotic Laxation and Motility: The high concentration of unabsorbed D-glucitol acts synergistically with structural fibers to increase intraluminal osmotic pressure, retaining fluid in the colon and accelerating peristaltic transit times.

Osteoblast Stimulation and Bone Matrix Preservation: High concentrations of phylloquinone combined with specific polyphenols downregulate osteoclast differentiation and enhance osteoblast activity, structurally fortifying trabecular bone microarchitecture.

Polyphenolic Attenuation of Systemic Oxidation: Dense chlorogenic and neochlorogenic acid fractions actively donate hydrogen atoms to neutralize highly reactive oxygen species, suppressing systemic inflammatory cytokines and protecting lipid cell membranes.

Potassium-Driven Vascular Hyperpolarization: Elevated bioavailable potassium ions activate smooth muscle cell membrane channels, promoting intracellular hyperpolarization that prompts vasodilation and a systemic down-regulation of arterial blood pressure.
precautionsIntro: Due to the unique biochemical presence of unabsorbed sugar alcohols and the physical concentration of specific carbohydrates, clinical monitoring is advised:
precautions: Sorbitol-Induced Osmotic Diarrhea and Gastrointestinal Distress: Rapid consumption of high quantities can overwhelm intestinal absorption capacity, leading to rapid fermentation by colonic bacteria and resulting in bloating, flatulence, and acute loose stools.

Thermodynamic Density and Adipose Homeostasis Strain: The dehydrated cellular matrix presents a highly concentrated caloric payload per unit mass, which can force a positive systemic energy balance and subsequent hepatic lipogenesis if portions are unmanaged.

Trace Acrylamide and Sulfite Hypersensitivity: Thermal processing can generate negligible trace levels of acrylamide, while commercial variations may utilize sulfur dioxide preservatives that can trigger severe bronchospastic reactions in asthmatic or sensitized individuals.
